players.product: AI colocation in retrofit data centers (NC-1 North Carolina 40 MW IT leased to Nscale; MTL-3 Montreal for Cerebras) plus GPU cloud services on NVIDIA B300 / Vera Rubin clusters

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-Q remaining performance obligations at June 30, 2026: $1,008,041 thousand in total, of which colocation services $932,895 thousand and cloud services $75,146 thousand; $57,680 thousand is scheduled for 2026 and $136,719 thousand for 2027.

WhiteFiber's 10-Q: in the second quarter of 2026 it executed a termination agreement with its Initial Customer. The agreement preserved $12.5 million of previously invoiced, unpaid receivables (fully collected by June 30, 2026) and obligates the customer to pay a fixed termination fee of $12.3 million, recognized as Q2 2026 revenue; after quarter-end the fee was amended to $15.7 million, which remains outstanding. A bad debt expense of approximately $2.2 million was recognized, and the GPUs were redeployed to other customers.
quarterly_data.figure: termination fee $12.3 million (Q2 revenue), amended to $15.7 million

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-Q: in May 2026 it entered into a two-year cloud services agreement with Hyperbolic Labs, Inc., with Modal Labs as the end customer and reference partner, deploying H200 GPUs from its existing owned fleet; total contract value is approximately $17 million, revenue commenced in June 2026, and no incremental GPU capital expenditures were required.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$17 million TCV over two years (Hyperbolic Labs / Modal Labs)

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-Q: purchases of and deposits made for property, plant and equipment were $344,712 thousand in the first six months of 2026 versus $130,961 thousand a year earlier; MTL-3's purchase closed on May 8, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 PP&E purchases and deposits $344,712 thousand vs $130,961 thousand
